claims.text: Controlled aging of a single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy can induce coherent, uniformly distributed nanoprecipitates.
Formation of these nanoprecipitates will improve the strength–plasticity combination relative to the as-cast or homogenized alloy.
An intermediate-temperature aging treatment lasting several hours can produce controlled precipitation.
Aging at approximately 600–800°C can promote precipitation without overaging.
The resulting nanoprecipitates will be coherent with and dispersed throughout the BCC matrix.
The nanoprecipitates obstruct dislocation motion and thereby raise strength.
Precipitate coherency permits effective dislocation bypass and storage mechanisms.
The proposed precipitate–dislocation interactions delay dislocation pile-up and premature failure.
The aged alloy will have higher yield strength than the untreated cast or homogenized alloy.
The aged alloy will have greater tensile ductility than the untreated cast or homogenized alloy.
The beneficial effect requires precipitates to remain coherent and to have an optimal size and distribution.
Excessive aging can coarsen the precipitates or cause loss of coherency.
Precipitate coarsening or loss of coherency may eliminate the improvement and reduce ductility.
Similar precipitate-strengthening mechanisms have been observed or established in other alloys.
The magnitude of the strength and plasticity changes and the optimal aging window depend sensitively on alloy composition and processing details.
Mechanical performance should be evaluated at room temperature under quasi-static strain rates.
